subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the remaining maxChars paragraph-boundary case be solved with explicit boundary metadata, a reserve-width chunk split, or accepted as a documented partial repair for this bug?
rationale: The current text-only patch cannot both keep every chunk within `maxChars` and preserve a consumed separator at an exact-boundary split; choosing the permanent seam contract affects the shared block-reply delivery path and the sibling PR.

options.title: Add boundary metadata
options.body: Carry paragraph-boundary semantics through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer so delivery can preserve the seam without over-limit text chunks.

options.title: Reserve width in size splits
options.body: Split earlier when a paragraph boundary follows so the separator can remain in-band, with tests proving no coalesced word-split regression.

options.title: Accept partial text-only repair
options.body: Land the common in-budget improvement and leave the exact-boundary overflow case tracked on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Add boundary metadata
recommendation.body: Carry paragraph-boundary semantics through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer so delivery can preserve the seam without over-limit text chunks.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest historical connection to both the block chunker and block-reply coalescer surfaces that need a seam-contract decision.
